task_name: The endpoint that reads gate 2 and runs the groom

rubric.result: The objective promises three things and each is produced by a line of backend/src/infrastructure/epic-groom-route.ts. (a) 'the cabin reads gate 2's rung': EpicGroomRoute.reading answers {status:'none'} with no held session and otherwise dispatches the six EpicGroomState members in #answerRead with a switch whose default is a `const exhaustive: never` throw — draft and awaiting-publication bare, groomable with milestone and plan.issues, groomed and authorised with milestone and issues. (b) 'with the key only it receives': the GET mints through key.forThePage({origin, host, site}) with site read from GateKey.SITE_HEADER, and spreads `key` only into the groomable and groomed bodies and only when minted !== null; the POST's first statement is key.holds(request.get(GateKey.HEADER)). (c) 'runs the groom': the POST invokes GroomEpic.execute with root and repository taken from held().conversation and answers status/milestone/issues. 'every refusal arrives as {code, detail}': 403 via Answer.refuse, the three refused rungs via EpicGroomRefusal + Answer.refuseAs, a PlanFailure via PlanCollapse.of in both handlers, and 405 with {code:'method-not-allowed', detail:'method not allowed'}. Nothing the objective promises is missing; the gap the previous verdict found was in what watched (b), and the test that watches it is now in the diff.

The **TDD:** line asks for it('the read hands the gate key only at a rung with something to press') — a groomable read with the page's own Origin carries key, an authorised one with the same Origin has no key field at all — with the boundary pair it('a post with no gate key is refused and the groom is never asked'). Both are in the diff with those exact names and the plan's exact assertions, unchanged from attempt 1: two servers on the same GateKey, both fetched with { Origin: RunningApi.ownOrigin(port) }, the groomable body asserted toEqual {status:'groomable', milestone, plan:{issues:[{order:1,title:'#1 First slice',labels:['type:feature']}]}, key: Keys.MINTED} and the authorised body toEqual an object with no key member (toEqual fails on an extra property, so 'no key field at all' is really pinned); the pair asserts 403, the literal {code:'gate-not-from-the-page', detail:'gate 2 answers only a request carrying the key the page was given'} and expect(groom.asked).toEqual([]). Same assertion, same input, same expected value. The two fetches added in attempt 2 are additional cases inside the same test, and they do not touch what the plan wrote down.

Compared name by name with the Contract (backend/src/infrastructure/epic-groom-route.ts) block, and unchanged from attempt 1. EpicGroomOutcome is Object.freeze'd with the six members and the six literals exactly as written (accepted, gate-not-from-the-page, no-coordinating-session, no-epic-spec, spec-not-frozen, spec-not-published). EpicGroomRoute.PATH = '/epic-groom', METHODS = 'GET, POST', RECORD = 'gate 2 groom'; static reading(held: CoordinatingSessions, read: ReadEpicGroom, key: GateKey): RequestHandler, static grooming(held: CoordinatingSessions, groom: GroomEpic, key: GateKey, stderr: (line: string) => void): RequestHandler, static refuseOtherMethods(request: Request, response: Response): void — same parameter names, same order, same types, same returns. The prose contract holds too: no JsonBody middleware (no body is read), root and repository out of holding.conversation, key on groomable and groomed only and only when minted, the key demanded before anything is asked, EpicGroomRefusal projecting the three refused rungs through Projection keyed on EpicGroomState, PlanFailure becoming PlanCollapse, one RECORD line to stderr after a successful groom. No Final text block existed to match.

Row by row. D-22 (the gates are the human's; an attempt is refused with an explicit code rather than obeyed) is the row this diff bears on hardest and it now has both halves implemented and measured: the POST refuses with gate-not-from-the-page at 403 before asking anything, and the GET mints the key only for the browser on this origin — the new bare fetch asserts that a request which is not the page receives a body with no key at all. D-6 (gate 2 is an act of the app): the groom is a press the program answers for. D-23 (the groom waits for the merge): spec-not-published is projected from AWAITING_PUBLICATION and refuses, touching nothing. D-11 (a yardstick is imported, never reimplemented): the route consumes ReadEpicGroom/GroomEpic and reuses GroomEpic.REFUSED instead of restating the refused partition. D-13 (no phase is stored): nothing is stored; every answer is the rung the query derived. D-10: both new files are TypeScript. D-7: nothing here writes to a pull request and there is no merge button. D-1, D-14, D-18, D-21, D-25 have no subject in this diff. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: epic-groom-route.ts is spec-freeze-route.ts rewritten for gate 2 — same Answer/Refusal/Projection/PlanCollapse idiom, same #answerRead switch with a `never` default, same conditional key spread, same refuseOtherMethods, same forThePage({origin, host, site}) call shape (spec-freeze-route.ts:93-97). The test file mirrors spec-freeze-route.test.ts's RunningApi (real express app with Browsers.turnAwayForeign on the GET, createServer, port 0 on 127.0.0.1, afterEach stopAll) and its Mother of named scenarios. The divergence that was the previous verdict's high finding is repaired and I checked the repair by reading GateKey and Browsers rather than by trusting the name: fromThePage sends only { 'Sec-Fetch-Site': 'same-origin' }, so Browsers.isOurOwnPage(undefined, '127.0.0.1:port') is false and the ONLY branch that can mint is `asked.site === GateKey.SAME_ORIGIN && Browsers.isOurOwnHost(asked.host)` — drop or blank `site: request.get(GateKey.SITE_HEADER)` and that assertion goes red on the missing `key`; fromElsewhere sends neither header, so minted is null and toEqual on a body with no key member fails the moment production hands a key to a curl. Both halves of the exemplar's case (spec-freeze-route.test.ts:296-324) are now measured. architecture.md 'One controller per endpoint': the route, its outcome vocabulary and its refusal projection travel in one new module and nothing else was put there; layer direction is right (infrastructure importing application and domain, domain importing nobody). boundaries.md: the projection outwards is exhaustive — the Projection raises for an unmapped rung and the switch's default is a `never` throw — and every code is declared explicitly beside its detail, none derived from a class name. decisions.md: the refused partition is imported (GroomEpic.REFUSED) rather than restated, and the same-origin rule stays inside GateKey. style.md: no comment or docstring, every identifier English, every function hangs off a class. domain.md: no tool noun. testing.md's controller row is honoured — use cases doubled by construction, assertions on the status and the literal body through a real listening server and a real client, and 'a refusal never reaches a double' asserted twice (groom.asked === [] on the 403, read.asked === [] on the 405). defects.md, its four rules: (1) closed vocabulary — EpicGroomOutcome and EpicGroomState are frozen vocabularies, the dispatch has no catch-all that guesses and the absence of a key is the absent property rather than a flag; nothing is classified by a loose string or a boolean; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: WirePlanIssue and WireIssue are typed records built in the last step before Answer.send, which decides nothing with them, and the use cases return EpicGroomRead/EpicGroomed value objects; (3) two fields that have to agree — none introduced: no sentinel stands for an absence (minted === null omits the property, milestone carries null), and the state/nullable-plan pairing behind `outcome.plan!` belongs to EpicGroomRead, shipped in task 4 and untouched here; (4) an error named for where it happens — no subject: the diff declares no error type, reusing PlanFailure/PlanCollapse. Delivery shape: the two new files change no existing signature and refusal-codes.test.ts only gains lines, so no call site is left on an old path. Declared and left out of the findings: `export type EpicGroomOutcomeValue` has no consumer in the tree, which is simplicity.md's 'a public symbol with no caller', but it is the one-line mirror every route vocabulary here already carries (SpecFreezeOutcomeValue included) and the exemplar the plan named is where it comes from.

The one pre-existing test file touched is backend/__tests__/infrastructure/refusal-codes.test.ts and the diff has no '-' line anywhere (634 insertions, 0 deletions across the three files). I read the whole file rather than the hunk: the guard is still expect(repeated.sort()).toEqual([...SharedOnPurposeAcrossRequestVocabularies.CODES].sort()), an equality and not a subtraction, so an undeclared collision still fails AND a declared-shared code that stops repeating still fails. Folding EpicGroomOutcome into RequestVocabularies.codes() widens the pool measured, and the declaration added is exactly the three the task names — gate-not-from-the-page, no-coordinating-session, no-epic-spec — with no fourth, leaving spec-not-frozen and spec-not-published measured as unique. Nothing was removed, relaxed or rewritten here or in the new file.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. The rung dispatch, the wire projection of plan issues and epic issues, the conditional key spread, the gate-key demand, the refusal Projection, the PlanCollapse path and the RECORD line all live in backend/src/infrastructure/epic-groom-route.ts; the test file only stands a real express server up, feeds the doubled use cases their answers and records what they were asked. Keys.MINTED is not a hard-coded expectation either: it is the hex of the deterministic buffer the real GateKey is constructed with, so it can only appear in a body because production called forThePage — which is exactly why the two new fetches measure a production line and not a fixture. Revert epic-groom-route.ts and all eight tests fail at import.

The diff writes the three paths **Files:** declares and nothing else: epic-groom-route.ts (create), epic-groom-route.test.ts (create), refusal-codes.test.ts (modify). There is no plan hunk, so there is no amendment to rule on — the **Tests:** list, the **TDD:** name and the **Verification:** commands all still read as the committed plan wrote them, and the repair was made inside them rather than by rewriting them. Attempt 2 adds exactly 13 lines over attempt 1 (621 -> 634 insertions): two fetches and their two toEqual blocks, all inside the existing gate-key test. Nothing else drifted. Inside the files every line traces to a sentence of the task: the Contract block accounts for the vocabulary, the two handlers, refuseOtherMethods and the RECORD; the prose for the per-rung bodies and the key spread; the eight tests are the eight the **TDD:** and **Tests:** lines name, with no ninth and none dropped. Nothing in ### Out of scope is touched — no plugin script, no --reconcile or Project v2, no dispatcher or gate 1 behaviour, no pull-request write, no repository column.

Eight new tests, measured on the three properties. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no randomness (Keys.RANDOM is Buffer.alloc(size, 7)), no sleep; the only network is loopback to a server this file starts on port 0, and the two fetches added in attempt 2 hit that same server with fixed headers. Isolated: every test builds its own CoordinatingSessions, doubles and server, the shared statics are frozen value objects and string constants, afterEach drains RunningApi.#started and closes every server, and no test needs an order or a fixed port — the two extra requests reuse groomablePort within their own test and the spy they hit is stateless with respect to the assertions. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on the status and the literal body that came back over a real socket from the real handler, plus what the doubled use case received; none survives reverting epic-groom-route.ts, and the two new ones do not survive blanking the `site` argument or the same-origin branch either. The finer half was read with control-tower-loop:test-driven-development loaded: its 'Minimal — One thing. "and" in name? Split it.' is now bent further, because 'the read hands the gate key only at a rung with something to press' also guarantees that the key reaches the page and not a curl, which the name does not say. I declare it here instead of reporting it: the **TDD:** line pins that name verbatim and ct-step's control greps the staged files for it, and the **Tests:** line closes the set at eight names, so neither renaming nor splitting was available to the implementer inside the plan — the same treatment item 5 gives a control that clashes with a document. The skill's checklist item 'Edge cases and errors covered' is what attempt 1 offended and it is now satisfied.
